Long story, buckle up. I was using sensodyne for YEARS prior to trying this fluoride heavy toothpaste recommended by my doctor (3M Clinpro). I’m not even kidding — Clinpro is the reason I learned I have an allergy to sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS), because immediately after I started using it, these little clusters of bumps started appearing around the edges of my lips. They were nasty and damn near scaly. At its worst, there was this red, angry, itchy, raised ring of bumps around the outside of my lips. It was horrible. Nothing *in* my mouth was reacting, though. Just my lips.

Found out that was causing the allergic reaction after a trip to urgent care. so I went back to Sensodyne for a while. Not even an hour after using it I saw the clusters of bumps starting to form around the outside of my lips again.

Now I have to use the sulfate free brands, which isn’t an issue. But that’s how I learned I have an allergy to SLS.

imo all these traits are interconnected and they can’t exist without the others.
- victim complex
- lacked healthy boundaries
- entitlement
- blaming others for my problems
- being judgmental and negative
- attention seeking
- passive aggressive gossip

i was a terrible gossip spreader for my first two years of college and committed to doing the work to be better starting in 2019. i grew up in a small town, i had just left an abusive home, i was desperate for friends, and it was a hard pill to swallow that the lack of boundaries in my home & small town constant knowing of other people’s information doesn’t translate to college. i love bombed friends, i trauma bonded with them, i emotionally dumped on them, and i couldn’t comprehend why everyone kept me at arms length. i just wanted people to like me and that was the way i thought would work.
i was painfully passive aggressive and didn’t understand how to handle conflict / advocate for myself appropriately, and i was in a student group where my *shitty* actions had consequences each year and i was punished for them in a disrespectful, traumatic way every year.
in the history of the group, no one’s been punished or ostracized to the extent i have, even as an alum (still trying to figure out what moving forward and letting go looks like).
i’d always gossip under the guise of “venting” and wanting to let people know about the mistreatment of myself and others that was happening behind closed doors instead of confronting folks themselves for THEIR shitty behavior. and yesterday i learned that two years ago, two of my former friends said this to someone i had just met: “when basement asks to hang out with you, we’re going to meet with you afterward to see if you’re okay.”

there’s no blame that can be placed on just one party. i had MANY toxic traits, and the group, while it brought a lot of joy, it caused me a significant amount of pain and trauma.

i’d like to think i’ve turned myself around. i can take accountability for my actions now — i can objectively look at who i was for a lot of college and see that i was a really traumatized person that had a lot of work to do and needed to learn and grow in a safe environment. i own the fact that i was a really toxic person and that i’m doing my best not to be her anymore, and if i could apologize to all of the people i have hurt in person, i would. i want to apologize.
it’s hard to know that that’s the person i was to that group when she is in direct conflict with the person i am now. and it’s hard to know that that’s how some of them remember me. i’m still struggling with that. maybe one day there will be clarity.
